sayLines.line: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 2). You can tell when someone's lying, scared, or hiding something. It's in the shoulders.
⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
📖 LEARNED: Research & Records (Level 2). Cross-reference sources — one account is a rumor, three are a pattern.

📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
📖 Your old life taught you things. 3 skills from your past — check your Journal.
📖 Your hands remember: knap a Stone knife (stone + vine) — the oldest tool there is. Find the stone.
📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Anh Anderson. Journalist. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Daughter's Drawing, Boot stone, Reading Glasses, Busker's harmonica, Carpenter's square. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. You
A woman, maybe 30s, with freckles: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
You tell the others you're heading out. Someone nods. "Come back before dark."
— DAY 1 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
Filled 1L (clean — Haven well). 3L carried (3kg). (-10 kcal hauling, 1 tick.) Cistern: 24L left.
"You haven't earned that yet," A person, maybe 40s, with thick glasses says. (Trust too low.)
A person, maybe 50s heads out for water. "The well won't fill itself." The pantry won't fill itself.
A person, maybe 30s heads out to check the snares. "Wire doesn't lie." Good kit is the difference out there.
A person, maybe 40s, with ink-stained fingers walks away from Haven. They don't look back.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut sets out to find A person, maybe 50s. "Won't be long." Company makes the road shorter.
A woman, maybe 20s walks away from Haven. They don't look back.
Iron cold. Even the ticks are shelved.
— MIDDAY — Honest work hours. Heat builds.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
A person, maybe 40s, with thick glasses looks at you flatly. "Why should I listen to you?" (Trust too low.)
📋 A person, maybe 30s wants to know what's by the creek. "Just look. Come back and tell me."
— DUSK — Animals stir again. Shadows lengthen.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
A person, maybe 40s, with thick glasses shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
A woman, maybe 30s, with freckles heads out for water. "Thirst doesn't negotiate. Going." The pantry won't fill itself.
A man, maybe 60s heads out for water. "Water first. Everything else waits." The pantry won't fill itself.
A woman, maybe 60s heads out for water. "Off to the well — back with a full skin." The pantry won't fill itself.
— NIGHT — Camp. Rest — or risk the dark.
Night settles. The fire is the whole world now. No watches posted. The dark feels bigger than it should.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
